newsitem.title: USA: US blue chips end firmer, flirt with record highs.
newsitem.headline: US blue chips end firmer, flirt with record highs.

text.p: U.S. blue chips flirted with record closing highs as buying in some recent favorites resumed, but a day after the Christmas holiday NYSE volume was the slowest for a full session so far in 1996.

"Maybe it's the Christmas spirit carrying over," mused Michael Metz, Oppenheimer and Co's chief investment strategist. On a more serious note, he said, "It's the usual amount of random noise in the last few sessions of the year. The biggest investors are already done for the year."
The Dow industrials rose 24 points to about 6546.68.
That left the blue chip index just shy of its record closing high of 6547.79 set on November 25.
The S&P 500 rose five to about 756, nearing its all-time high finish of 757.03 set on November 25.
The Nasdaq Composite added seven to about 1295, still well short of its December 9 record of 1316.27.

Winners outpaced losers 15-8 on NYSE volume of about 253 million shares, the slowest full session of trading so far in 1996. Volume fell below the 258 million shares recorded August 30, which was previously the lowest volume for a full session this year.
U.S. financial markets were closed Wednesday, Christmas Day.
Tuesday's Christmas Eve NYSE volume of 167 million shares was notched during an abbreviated session.

Analysts said blue chips benefitted as some mutual fund managers did last-minute sprucing up of their portfolios before year's end. They expected similarly lethargic overall activity until after the New Year. "I don't think we'll get much action for the rest of the year with the holidays this week and next week (with New Year's Day on Wednesday). Brokerages and investment houses are minimally staffed," said Ed Nicoski, a Piper Jaffray technical analyst.

Technology stocks were again a favored sector, with Motorola rising 2-3/4 to 63-1/4, Micron adding 1-1/4 to 31-1/4, Compaq Computer up 1-1/8 to 75-3/4, Intel rising 1-1/8 to 136-5/8 and Microsoft up 5/8 to 85-1/2.

Among individual issues, AT&T rose 1-1/2 to 43, boosted by the Federal Communications Commission's proposal for long-distance access charge reform. The FCC's proposal to trim the $23 billion long-distance companies pay to local service providers in access fees would benefit AT&T and other long distance providers, industry analysts said.
Culbro surged 4-1/4 to 61-7/8.
The company plans to publicly sell shares of its General Cigar Holdings unit.
American Express lost 2-1/4 to 56-7/8 and General Electric added 1-1/4 to 103-1/4 after GE reiterated that it was not interested in buying American Express. AmEx declined to comment on market rumors.
Many global stock markets were closed for the holidays. U.K., German and some other European markets were closed for Boxing Day. The Hong Kong stock market was also closed.
The S&P 500 rose 4.79 to 755.82.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 6.94 to 1294.57.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
